name: Question 13
problem: A particle $P$ moves along a counterclockwise circular path centered at $O$ in the $xy$-plane with a constant angular velocity of $2\,\text{rad/s}.$ Given that the particle is located at $(3,0)$ when $t=0,$ find the acceleration of the particle at $t=\frac{\pi }{6}$ seconds.
worked_solution:
The position function of a particle moving in a circular path of radius $a$ in the $xy$-plane with a constant angular velocity $\omega $ is given by

$$
r(t)=a(\operatorname{cos}⁡\omega t\,i+\operatorname{sin}⁡\omega t\,j),
$$

where it is assumed that the circle is centered at $O,$ and the particle is at the position $(a,0)$ when $t=0.$

In our case, we have $a=3$ and $\omega =2\text{ rad/s},$ so we get that the position function is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =3(\operatorname{cos}⁡2t\,i+\operatorname{sin}⁡2t\,j).\end{aligned}
$$

We find the velocity and acceleration vectors by differentiating. We get

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =(3(\operatorname{cos}⁡2t\,i+\operatorname{sin}⁡2t\,j))^{′} \\  & =-6\operatorname{sin}⁡2t\,i+6\operatorname{cos}⁡2t\,j \\ a(t) & =(-6\operatorname{sin}⁡2t\,i+6\operatorname{cos}⁡2t\,j)^{′} \\  & =-12\operatorname{cos}⁡2t\,i-12\operatorname{sin}⁡2t\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we find the acceleration vector at $t=\frac{\pi }{6},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}a(\frac{\pi }{6}) & =-12\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\cdot \frac{\pi }{6})\,i-12\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\cdot \frac{\pi }{6})\,j \\  & =-12\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{3})\,i-12\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{3})\,j \\  & =-\frac{12}{2}\,i-\frac{12\sqrt{3}}{2}\,j \\  & =-6\,i-6\sqrt{3}\,j\end{aligned}
$$

Question 13
?

A particle P moves along a counterclockwise circular path centered at O in the xy-plane with a constant angular velocity of 2rad/s. Given that the particle is located at (3,0) when t=0, find the acceleration of the particle at t=π6 seconds.

a
−6i−6j
b
−6i
c
−63i+3j
d
−123i−12j
e
−6i−63j
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

The position function of a particle moving in a circular path of radius a in the xy-plane with a constant angular velocity ω is given by r(t)=a(cos⁡ωti+sin⁡ωtj), where it is assumed that the circle is centered at O, and the particle is at the position (a,0) when t=0.

In our case, we have a=3 and ω=2 rad/s, so we get that the position function is given by r(t)=3(cos⁡2ti+sin⁡2tj).

We find the velocity and acceleration vectors by differentiating. We get

v(t)=(3(cos⁡2ti+sin⁡2tj))′=−6sin⁡2ti+6cos⁡2tja(t)=(−6sin⁡2ti+6cos⁡2tj)′=−12cos⁡2ti−12sin⁡2tj.

Finally, we find the acceleration vector at t=π6, as follows: a(π6)=−12cos⁡(2⋅π6)i−12sin⁡(2⋅π6)j=−12cos⁡(π3)i−12sin⁡(π3)j=−122i−1232j=−6i−63j
